DILG .44 Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City wyyw.dilq.qov.ph OPINION NO. SO MAY 15 2025 ATTY. FRANCIS LORENZ N. MAGBUHOS 3F 155 EDSA Building Barangay Wack-Wack, Mandaluyong City Dear Atty. Magbuhos: We write in reference to your earlier letter requesting this Department's Legal Opinion conceming the propriety of Administrative Abatement or issuance of a Demolition Permit over an abandoned Barangay Senior Citizen Center situated over a real property registered in the name of a private individual. Culled from your letter are the following factual antecedents: A request for the issuance of Demolition Permit of the abandoned Barangay Senior Citizen was filed by your clients, Spouses Maynard Nueva and Kirr Jane Nueva (the "Spouses Nueva"). The Abandoned Center occupies the front portion of Spouses Nueva's residential property in Barangay Tambo Malaki, Indang, Cavite, registered in the name of the Spouses Nueva, as evidenced by Transfer of Certificate Title No. 057-2017012544 The subject Property is previously declared in the name of Anatano Herrera Nueva. During Anatano's stint as the Punong Barangay of Tambo Malaki, he lent the portion of the property to be used by the Barangay, until a Barangay Hall is constructed in a permanent location. o The property is later on transferred to Maynard's father, Frediswindo Nueva, and eventually transferred to the Spouses Nueva. In all those years, the annual real property taxes due on the Property including the portion occupied by the Abandoned Center are all paid by Mr. Anatano Nueva, Mr. Frediswindo Nueva, and now, the Spouses Nueva The Abandoned Center previously housed the Barangay Health Center. However, when a Barangay Hall was constructed in its present location, the Barangay Health Center was abandoned as all the services of the barangay are held at the new Barangay Hall. Since the Abandoned Center is no longer used by the Barangay, Spouses Nueva applied for a Demolition Permit so they can finally use the front portion of their driveway. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Punong Barangay of Tambo Malaki, Cornelio Salazar, objected to the issuance of the Demolition permit, claiming that the property was already donated to the barangav. On the other hand, the legal counsel of the barangay, Atty. Domingo Jan Reola, disclaims the "donation" and hinges the barangay's claim on prescription. It is your position that the issuance of a Demolition Permit is proper based on the following grounds: i. There can be no property issue considering the indefeasibility of the Certificate of Title issued in the name of Spouses Nueva. ii. The Abandoned Center is indeed abandoned and not used by Barangay Tambo, as evidenced by its deteriorating condition. iii. All functions of the Barangay are centralized in the current Barangay Hall; and iv. The Abandoned Center is not among the inventory of properties owned by the Local Government Unit. At the outset, this Department takes particular note that the instant issue fundamentally involves a factual dispute that is beyond the purview of the Department. It is our submission that the pivotal resolution of the subject issue hinges on the determination of the nature of the property in question. In this regard, please be apprised that since the matter involves a dispute over land ownership, the same falls squarely within the purview of the courts' jurisdiction. This Department is not clothed with the power to settle land disputes. It is respectfully opined that the matter should be settled before the court of competent jurisdiction by filing the appropriate action. Accordingly, we shall defer from taking cognizance of the matter as it is justiciable in nature, following this Department's policy of non-intervention in matters beyond the ambit of its mandate and competence as enunciated in its Memorandum Order No. 2010-02 dated 17 September 2010, thus: "[All] concerned are hereby advised that the Department shall not act on queries of the following kinds, to wit: 1. Those containing facts that are justiciable in nature. Justiciable issues are those that require adiudicptiqn the of law as tp who between the opposing parties has the better right given controversy; 2. Those presumptively valid acts, e.g., enacted ordinances, consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar instances; 3. Those that are litis pendencia or pending litigation, except when the court itself requests for the opinion. In the event that an opinion has been rendered by the Department and its field officers without knowledge or information that page 2 of 3

a case involving the issues raised in the query is pending in court, such opinion shall automatically be deemed ineffective; and 4. Those that are cognizable by other agencies of the government." We hope to have guided you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: . ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LRALLD/JVPR/jam Page 3 of 3
